<issue>
Need to flag "verse" used as a verb related to "versus"
The English word **versus** is a preposition, meaning it can come before nouns and noun phrases.

But some younger and/or foreign speakers of English treat it as a verb:
- We were having that discussion last night about train ride **verse** plane ride.
- A game of Morra, with 3 different AI you can **verse** against.
- This will make you switch to Smite and Fanatisim if you are **versing** a particular boss.
- Welcome to rock, paper, scissors, where you will **verse** a computer, and the first one to win 3 rounds, wins
- In my last 5 games as a solo I have **versed** both duos and trios in every game.
- Newer players never **versed** Torch in his OP state so its really funny cos they dont even know what his kit does fully, since they never **vs** him.
- I want the function to take input from the user who will type in the name of 2 teams they want to **verse** each other
- I'm making my first ever project which is a dice game in pygame where you press the y key to roll a dice and you **verse** the computer
- I'm writing a code where I am **versing** the computer.
- The player is **versing** a PC and the results of the game are based on the 2 values.
- Is there any disadvantages to it **verses** the standard pipeline or the semantic proposal?
- Utilizing this method you can see how many adoptable dogs are house trained in the U.S. **verses** those that are not.
- Balancing the amount of work on it **verses** other work, but should now be able to make progress.
- That 10% could ruin that extension even though there might be 100k actually using it **verses** only 4k from the 80% of 5k extension.
- Teams in Group1 does NOT **verse** teams in Group3
- Teams in Group1 **verses** every other team in Group 1 twice (Eg. 1v2, 2v1, 1v3, 3v1, 1v4, 4v1, 1v5, 5v1.....)
- This same rule applies to teams in Group3 as they **verse** other teams in Group3
- Teams in Group2 **verse** every other team once.
- I also added Lichess api functionality so that you can **verse** the bot online.
- This is a Tic Tac Toe bot, where you can **verse** it either starting or going second.
- If you want to manually test improvement, you can **verse** your current bot against an older version and see who comes out on top.
- A web game where you **verse** your friends and test your reflexes.
- You will be **versing** the computer, Good luck!
- ... the team they are **versing**.

When misused this way it is spelled **"verses"** in the third-person singular present, which is a different English word, a plural noun, so doesn't invoke spellcheck.
- **"versed"** also passes spellcheck because it's also a different word, most commonly seen in the phrase "well-versed".
- **"verse"**, used as the lemma is of course also a word, a singular noun.
- **"versing"** is archaic. We can probably remove it from the dictionary.
- **"verses"** may be used as a verb form and as a misspelling for the preposition.

Because most of the inflections are already English words, context will be essential to disambiguate whether it's an error or legitimate use.

Suggested replacements could be: **face**, **challenge**, **play against**, **compete against**.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Harper grammar checker?), find how linters are structured, e.g. a simple phrase/word-based linter with a few examples, and how they're registered (lib.rs) and tested. Report file paths, and show a small example linter file (e.g. one using ExprLinter or a pattern with a replacement) in full, plus the registration lines in lint_group.rs for it.

content.content: {"summary":"Harper linters live in harper-core/src/linting/, one file per rule. Each rule is a struct that implements ExprLinter. A rule is registered in three places: `mod x;` in mod.rs, a `use` in lint_group.rs, and an `insert_expr_rule!` line in lint_group.rs. Unit tests sit in a #[cfg(test)] module at the bottom of each rule file. I did not find any `pub use` line for Addicting in mod.rs, so the lib.rs registration you asked about is unconfirmed. Addicting (addicting.rs) is the example; I printed it in full but only summarise it here.","findings":["Example linter: harper-core/src/linting/addicting.rs. It defines `pub struct Addicting { expr: LongestMatchOf }` and builds the expression in `impl Default`, using SequenceExpr::aco(\"addicting\"), then_whitespace, All, and unless(...) to skip reflexive and object pronouns.","`impl ExprLinter for Addicting` has `type Unit = Chunk`, `fn expr(&self) -> &dyn Expr`, `fn match_to_lint(&self, toks, src) -> Option<Lint>` and `fn description(&self) -> &str`. match_to_lint returns a Lint with span: tok.span, lint_kind: LintKind::Style, a Suggestion::replace_with_match_case(\"addictive\", original) and a message.","Registration, step 1: mod.rs:7 has `mod addicting;`.","Registration, step 2: lint_group.rs:16 has `use super::addicting::Addicting;`.","Registration, step 3: lint_group.rs:603 has `insert_expr_rule!(Addicting, true);`. The true means the rule is enabled by default.","The insert_expr_rule! macro is defined at lint_group.rs:564-570. It calls out.add_chunk_expr_linter(stringify!($rule), $rule::default()) and then out.config.set_rule_enabled(...). Variants exist: insert_expr_rule_with_dict! (line 573, calls ::new(dictionary)) and insert_expr_rule_with_dialect! (line 582, calls ::new(dialect)).","lint_group.rs also merges weir_rules::lint_group() and phrase_set_corrections::lint_group() at lines 590-591. Many simple phrase corrections are defined there rather than as their own files.","Tests: each rule file has a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` that imports helpers from crate::linting::tests: assert_suggestion_result(text, Linter::default(), expected), assert_lint_count(text, linter, n) and assert_no_lints(text, linter). #[ignore = \"reason\"] marks known false positives.","Other test locations: harper-core/tests/ contains linters.rs, run_tests.rs, snapshot.rs, pos_tags.rs, plus test_sources and text directories."],"confidence":0.8}

input.instruction: In /testbed/harper-core/src/expr/sequence_expr.rs list the public method names/signatures for: word_set / then_word_set / aco / t_ws / then_whitespace / then_any_of / then_determiner / then_pronoun. Also show the line in linting/mod.rs where `mod addicting;` is.

content.content: {"summary":"Found all eight methods in sequence_expr.rs. Six are written out as plain `pub fn` items. `then_determiner` and `then_pronoun` are generated by the `gen_then_from_is!` macro. `mod addicting;` is at linting/mod.rs:7.","findings":["sequence_expr.rs:103 `pub fn aco(word: &'static str) -> Self` (an associated constructor with no `self`)","sequence_expr.rs:108 `pub fn word_set(words: &'static [&'static str]) -> Self` (also a constructor)","sequence_expr.rs:175 `pub fn then_any_of(mut self, exprs: Vec<Box<dyn Expr>>) -> Self`","sequence_expr.rs:197 `pub fn then_word_set(self, words: &'static [&'static str]) -> Self`","sequence_expr.rs:207 `pub fn then_whitespace(self) -> Self`","sequence_expr.rs:212 `pub fn t_ws(self) -> Self`","`then_pronoun` has no literal `pub fn` line. It comes from `gen_then_from_is!(pronoun);` at sequence_expr.rs:559. The macro, defined at lines 17-25, expands to `pub fn then_pronoun(self) -> Self`, which calls `then_kind_where` with `is_pronoun`.","`then_determiner` is likewise generated by `gen_then_from_is!(determiner);` at sequence_expr.rs:596, giving `pub fn then_determiner(self) -> Self`. The macro also generates `then_optional_*` variants.","linting/mod.rs:7: `mod addicting;`"],"confidence":0.95}
